The device features a large, heavy-duty circular housing with an integrated central cooling fan. Arranged radially around the circumference are multiple modular pneumatic brake calipers with finned heat sinks to maximize heat dissipation. A Pneumatic brake is a type of friction brake in which compressed air pressing on a piston is used to apply pressure to the brake pad needed to stop the moving / rotating object. ### Operating Principle The operating principle is similar to that of a brake calliper used in the automotive sector, where the sensitivity depends solely on the capacity of the calliper to reset, in such a way that the increase in pressure is directly proportional to the desired torque. It is suitable to use in printing, on paper slitters from rolls to sheets and reminder slitters, metal, packaging, wire & cable industry, textile industry & all other applications requiring medium / high tension throughout the unwinding / rewinding process. --- ### Key Features - Modular calliper system. - Unrivalled level of performance. - Easy to install, repair & service. - Flexibility & rapid adaptation to variation in torque / pressure. - Less components, reduced maintenance. - High heat dissipation in order to prolong life of brake. - Customizable. (Number of pads, callipers, size of hub, fan type). - Excellent brake pad life. - High sensitivity. --- ### AX Series Model Specifications **Code for Selection:** `AX [Bore Diameter] . The diagram includes dimensional variables such as 'D' (Diameter of the disc), 'd', and pad center measurements. It is used in applications requiring low or medium braking force. ### Features - One or more callipers can be installed on the brake disc. - Each calliper can be activated or deactivated based on required Torques, making the system highly flexible. - Highly flexible. **To calculate the dynamic torque (Cd) of the AX calliper, use the following formula:** Cd = Rm × F **Where:** - **F** = Thrust force of the caliper on the disc's surface including the friction of the pad - **Rm** = Medium radius \[m\], calculated as: Rm = (d - Mp) / 2000 - **D** (or **d**) = Diameter of the discs \[mm\] - **Mp** = Pad center \[mm\]\* - **Cd** = Dynamic torque \[Nm\] --- **Global Reach:** Canada, USA, Germany, Turkey, China, Morocco, Nepal, Bangladesh, UAE, West Indies, Thailand, Nigeria, Kenya, Sri Lanka, Singapore, Zambia, South Africa. *NOTE: The information in this catalogue reflects the current technical specifications at the time of print.
